topic: Straight line and written down value methods
question: What is depreciation? Distinguish between the straight line method and the written down value method of charging depreciation.
sources: AS 10, Property, Plant and Equipment (issued by ICAI) - depreciation
Standard accounting principles on depreciation methods

points.label: Meaning of depreciation
points.description: Depreciation is the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset (cost less residual value) over its useful life; it reflects the using up of the asset's economic benefits.
points.basis: AS 10, definitions of depreciation and depreciable amount

points.label: Basis of calculation
points.description: Under the straight line method depreciation is charged on the original cost (depreciable amount); under the written down value method it is charged at a fixed rate on the reducing book value at the start of each year.
points.basis: Accounting principle: computation under straight line and written down value methods

points.label: Amount of yearly charge
points.description: Straight line gives an equal charge every year; written down value gives a higher charge in early years that falls year after year.
points.basis: AS 10, depreciation methods (straight-line gives a constant charge, diminishing balance a decreasing charge)

points.label: Asset value at end of life
points.description: Under straight line the book value can be brought down to zero or to residual value; under written down value the book value never becomes zero.
points.basis: Accounting principle: features of written down value method

points.label: Suitability
points.description: Straight line suits assets whose benefits are used evenly over time (such as leases or patents); written down value suits assets like plant and machinery where repairs rise and benefits fall as the asset ages. The method chosen should reflect the pattern in which the asset's benefits are expected to be used.
points.basis: AS 10, depreciation method should reflect the expected pattern of consumption of future economic benefits
